children: Grades were mixed on Wednesday, dealers said, after US crude stocks fell while Saudi Aramco
ramped up crude loadings in the Gulf.
U.S. crude stocks fell amid strong exports while gasoline and distillate inventories rose last week, the Energy Information Administration said on Wednesday.
Crude inventories fell by 640,000 barrels to 423.4 million barrels in the week ended September 11, the EIA said, compared with analysts' expectations in a Reuters poll for a 1.6 million-barrel draw.

Saudi Arabia is offering more loadings of crude oil to Asian refiners via ship-to-ship transfer off Oman's Sohar port. State oil company Saudi Aramco was offering its flagship Arab Light grade, as well as Arab Medium and Arab Heavy, to term buyers in Asia for loading off Sohar, the sources said, which is outside the Strait of Hormuz.

Aramco is ramping up those STS transfers after drone attacks damaged the East-West pipeline, which the company has been using to divert crude to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, people familiar with the matter said.
Light Louisiana Sweet for October delivery rose 13 cents to a midpoint of a $5.38 premium and was seen bid and offered between a $5.00 and $5.75 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures
Mars Sour rose $2 to a midpoint of a $7 premium and was seen bid and offered between a $6.90 and $7.10 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures
WTI Midland fell 10 cents to a midpoint of a $1.40 premium and was seen bid and offered between a $1.30 and $1.50 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures
West Texas Sour was steady at a midpoint of a 20-cent discount and was seen bid and offered between a​ discount of 40 cents and parity to U.S. crude futures
WTI at East Houston, also known as MEH, traded between a $1.90 and $2.10 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures
fell $2.92 to settle at $105.83 a barrel
futures fell $3.40 to settle at $102.43 a barrel
The Brent/WTI spread widened 24 cents to last trade at minus $8.24, after hitting a high of minus $7.86 and a low of minus $8.67
